name: projected_extreme_apex_grouping
mechanism: Color the two horizontal screen extremes L/R blue and the other three existing vertices T/F/B red. This targets mistaking screen extremes for the two bipyramid apices, assigning the blue pair 5 and red triple1 and reporting13. Every marker coincides with a frozen existing vertex; no graph edge, face, or number changes.
primary_math_proof: The six faces are TLF,TFR,TRL,BLF,BFR,BRL. Equal totals for the top three give L=F=R. Given L=5, all equatorial vertices are5. Comparing TLF with BLF gives T=B; given T=1, B=1. Total is3*5+2*1=17 uniquely. The valid graph classes are T/B and L/F/R, and the colored screen-based grouping is not a number equality condition.

marker_roles.role: Given 5 vertex at left screen extreme: blue anchor for false horizontal apex pair.
Right screen extreme: blue companion, inviting value5 as the other supposed apex.
Given 1 vertex: red anchor for false three-member equatorial group.
Projected central/front vertex: red member of the false equatorial triple.
Lower true apex: red member of the false equatorial triple.
